stories.name: Hristina Hristova, Clemens Blattert, Bogdan Candrea, Janine Schweier (WSL Forest Team)
stories.story_summary: A team of researchers at the Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research (WSL) used an Insta360 Pro 2 camera to capture 360-degree video transects of forest plots for automated 3D reconstruction. Their videogrammetry method — detailed in a paper published in Ecological Informatics on September 8, 2025 — achieved tree position errors of 5.2–18.8 cm and diameter at breast height (DBH) errors of 0.9–1.9 cm, demonstrating that a single-operator walk-through with an Insta360 Pro 2 can rival or complement traditional terrestrial LiDAR for forest inventory.
stories.why_it_matters: Swiss federal forest scientists used the Insta360 Pro 2 in a peer-reviewed methodology that could replace or supplement expensive LiDAR equipment for forest inventory across Europe — opening a completely new professional/scientific market segment for Insta360.
stories.source_quote: A videogrammetry approach to reconstruct 3D point clouds in forest environments leveraging an Insta 360 Pro 2 acquisition setup
stories.verification_note: Insta360 Pro 2 appears in the paper title ('A study using Insta 360 Pro 2') and in search snippets describing the methodology. Paper published September 8, 2025 in Ecological Informatics (Elsevier). Source URL returns 403 on WebFetch (consistent Elsevier/ScienceDirect bot-detection; publicly accessible to humans). Authors confirmed at WSL via ResearchGate profiles and WSL DORA repository. Not on exclusion list. Not in previous results.

stories.name: Paola Di Giuseppantonio Di Franco, Francesca Dolcetti, Matteo Baraldo (REPLACE Project, University of Essex)
stories.location: Colchester, Essex, UK (fieldwork: Amatrice & Accumoli, Italy)
stories.story_summary: Archaeologist and digital heritage researcher Paola Di Giuseppantonio Di Franco and colleagues at the University of Essex used an Insta360 ONE RS (1-inch 360 edition) mounted on a 120 cm selfie stick to conduct walking interviews in Amatrice and Accumoli — towns devastated by the 2016 central Italy earthquake. Over 20 hours of 360-degree video footage was captured during place-centric ethnographic fieldwork for the UKRI Future Leader Fellowship project REPLACE (Rebuilding a Sense of Place). A paper analysing the methodology was published in Visual Communication (SAGE) in 2025 (doi: 10.1177/14703572251364346).
stories.why_it_matters: UK academic researchers used the Insta360 ONE RS in post-disaster ethnographic fieldwork in earthquake-devastated Italian communities — combining social science, cultural heritage, and immersive 360 documentation in a UKRI-funded project with ongoing 2025 publications.
stories.source_quote: using a 360-degree camera (Insta360 One RS, 1-inch 360 edition) mounted on a 120 cm selfie stick and controlled via a smartphone
stories.verification_note: Insta360 ONE RS explicitly named in multiple search snippets from SAGE and Google Scholar results. Paper published 2025 in Visual Communication.
